title: Judged Useless, Queried Anyway: Tool-Using Agents Rarely Turn Their Own Evidence Judgments into Stopping Decisions
abstract: The paper separates how tool-using agents judge evidence from what they do with those judgments under controlled source failures. Across seven tested agents, failing-source results are usually judged useless while stopping often does not follow those judgments. A harness-enforced rule that forces answering after five consecutive useless judgments makes stopping evidence-responsive and improves failing-source behavior.
